title: Iterator Consumers
concept: Iterator consumers materialize lazy iterator chains into concrete results — collect to Vec, fold to a single value, sum to a number.
why: Adapters set up the pipeline. Consumers run it. Without consumers, your beautiful adapter chain does nothing.
theory:
## From Iterator to Value

### collect — Gather into a Collection
```xiom
let nums = Vec[Int](); nums.push(1); nums.push(2); nums.push(3);
let doubled: Vec[Int] = nums.iter().map(|n| n * 2).collect();
// doubled = [2, 4, 6]
```

### fold — Reduce to a Single Value
```xiom
let sum = nums.iter().fold(0, |acc, n| acc + n);
// sum = 6
```

`fold` takes an initial accumulator and a function that combines the accumulator with each element.

### Common Consumers

| Consumer | Returns | Example |
|----------|---------|---------|
| .collect() | Vec[T], Set[T], Map[K,V] | .collect() |
| .fold(init, f) | Any type | .fold(0, |a,x| a + x) |
| .sum() | Numeric sum | .sum() |
| .count() | Int (element count) | .count() |
| .for_each(f) | () (side effects) | .for_each(|x| println(x)) |
| .all(p) | Bool | .all(|x| x > 0) |
| .any(p) | Bool | .any(|x| x < 0) |
| .find(p) | Option[T] | .find(|x| x > 10) |
| .nth(n) | Option[T] | .nth(2) |
| .last() | Option[T] | .last() |

### Multiple Consumers Per Iterator
```xiom
let iter = nums.iter();
let sum = iter.sum();  // Consumes iter
// iter.next();  // ERROR: iter was consumed by sum
```

### Consumer + Adapter Pipeline
```xiom
let avg = nums.iter()
  .filter(|n| n % 2 == 0)  // Keep evens
  .fold((0, 0), |(sum, count), n| (sum + n, count + 1));
// avg.0 / avg.1 = average of evens
```
syntax_ref:
// Adapter → Adapter → Consumer
iter.filter(p).map(f).collect()    // Collect to Vec
iter.filter(p).fold(0, |a,x| a+x)  // Reduce to value
iter.map(f).sum()                  // Sum numbers
iter.filter(p).count()             // Count matches
tips: Consumers are the final step — they trigger the computation of the lazy chain
fold is the most powerful consumer — you can implement sum, count, collect, and more with it
An iterator can only be consumed ONCE — plan your pipeline accordingly
Use all/any for boolean checks, find/nth/last for element retrieval
common_mistakes: Trying to use an iterator after consuming it — it's gone
Using collect() without specifying the target type — sometimes needs type annotation
Using fold when a simpler consumer (sum, count, any) would suffice
